correctness.rationale: For the defined stationary occupancy Q_t, f(z)=e^(−αz)/2. A reset in (0,t] makes the terminal state conditionally independent of the initial one. Conditional covariance is therefore e^(−rt) times the covariance of the initial threshold and its free Gaussian evolution. Independent Poisson marking gives the bivariate-Poisson law, and total covariance adds the variance of the conditional mean, θ/8. For the Gaussian calculation, scale lengths by α and set G∼N(0,2u). Conditional on G=g, integration of f(z) times the shifted Laplace tail gives e^g/8 for g≤0 and 1/2−(3/8+g/4)e^(−g) for g≥0. Their normal average gives the claimed second integral, using E[e^(−G);G>0]=F(u)/2 and E[G e^(−G);G>0]=√(u/π)−uF(u). Exponential memorylessness above a threshold gives the first integral (1+F(u))/(4α). Strict decay follows by comparing Gaussian threshold probabilities for starting positions on opposite sides of the threshold; the large-lag expansion gives the stated prefactor. At zero lag the two variances are θ/2 and 3θ/8. Given almost every anchor configuration the stationary conditional path process is ergodic (finite-cylinder mixing and approximation), and Q_t has finite conditional mean. The ergodic theorem yields the anchor sum; its Poisson Laplace functional gives all cumulants and the first-anchor decomposition gives the Dickman identity. Independent nested Gaussian quadrature at D=r=ρ=1 produced conditional covariances 0.22294816322803, 0.038545082450942 and 0.00075536467487785 at u=0.2,1.5,5, agreeing with the formula; the frozen script was inspected, not run. Scope clarification: since the displacement starts stationary, Q₀ need not be zero; the occupancy-balance current since that stationary time origin would instead be Q_t−Q₀. The proof establishes the finding for the explicitly defined occupancy only.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: At fixed rate the mean square deviation of the time average from the anchor mean is O(1/T) by the covariance integral. Along T=n² this gives almost-sure convergence by Chebyshev and Borel–Cantelli, which extends to all T by nonnegativity of occupancy and (n+1)²/n²→1. The resulting mean is the Poisson sum of e^(−αz)/2; exponential spacing supplies exactly the standard Dickman fixed point after doubling. The joint law is the known marking formula with the already matched coefficient.
